findings.title: Async legacy writes derive their timeout context from the (soon-to-be-canceled) request context
findings.body: In Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection, the background goroutine does `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, 10*time.Second, ...)` where the outer `ctx` is the original request context. In the k8s apiserver/net-http stack, the request context is typically canceled as soon as the HTTP handler returns (which happens right after the main Storage write succeeds and the goroutine is spawned). As a result, the derived child context used for the async Legacy write is very likely already canceled (or about to be) by the time the goroutine runs, causing the 'safety measure' legacy write to fail with context-canceled errors almost every time instead of actually mirroring data to legacy storage. The context passed into the goroutine should be detached from the parent's cancellation (e.g. via `context.WithoutCancel`) before applying the new timeout, while still carrying trace/log values.

findings.title: Async legacy Update uses the raw UpdatedObjectInfo instead of the object actually persisted to Storage
findings.body: Previously, Mode3's Update fetched the old object, resolved `objInfo.UpdatedObject`, and explicitly wrapped the resolved object before writing to Legacy, guaranteeing Legacy received exactly what was written to Storage. The new implementation calls `d.Storage.Update(...)` and then, asynchronously, calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the same unresolved `objInfo`. Since `objInfo.UpdatedObject` is re-evaluated independently inside Legacy's own Update call (against Legacy's own 'old' object, which can have a different resourceVersion/content than Storage's), the final object written to Legacy can diverge from what Storage has, or the update can fail outright (e.g. on resourceVersion conflict checks), defeating the purpose of the safety-net replication.

findings.title: Storage.Create failure incorrectly recorded via recordLegacyDuration
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` even though this is a Storage (not Legacy) failure. The success branch correctly calls `d.recordStorageDuration`. This mislabels the dual-writer metrics, making it look like a Legacy error occurred when it was actually a Storage error, corrupting any dashboards/alerts used to gauge readiness for progressing dual-write modes.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses object name instead of resource Kind as the label
findings.body: On success, `d.recordStorageDuration(false, mode3Str, name, method, startStorage)` passes the per-request object `name` where every other call site in this file passes `options.Kind`. This both mislabels the metric (wrong semantic value for the 'kind' parameter) and risks high-cardinality Prometheus labels if `name` is used as a label value, since resource names are unbounded unlike Kind.

findings.title: Storage.Update failure incorrectly recorded via recordLegacyDuration
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Update` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startStorage)` instead of `d.recordStorageDuration`, mirroring the same mislabeling bug as in Create. This pollutes dual-write metrics by attributing Storage failures to Legacy.

findings.title: DeleteCollection async legacy call duration recorded via recordStorageDuration
findings.body: Inside the goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, the resulting duration/error is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, mode3Str, options.Kind, method, startLegacy)` instead of `d.recordLegacyDuration`. This mixes Legacy timing/error data into the Storage metric series, making it impossible to accurately monitor Legacy write reliability for DeleteCollection in mode 3.

findings.title: Errors from async Legacy writes are no longer logged
findings.body: In Create, Update, Delete, and DeleteCollection, the background goroutine that performs the Legacy write only records a metric (`d.recordLegacyDuration(...)`) when the Legacy call fails; there is no `log.Error` call anywhere in these goroutines. The previous implementation explicitly logged failures such as 'unable to create object in legacy storage'. Now, failures of the async safety-net write are silent except via metrics, making it much harder to diagnose why Legacy storage has drifted out of sync with Storage.

findings.title: Delete's context logger omits the per-request fields set on `log`
findings.body: In `Delete`, a `log` variable is built with `WithValues("name", name, "kind", options.Kind, "method", method)`, but the context is updated with `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` (the bare, field-less logger) rather than `log`. Every other method in this file (Create, Get, List, Update, DeleteCollection) correctly injects the enriched `log` into the context. As a result, any code downstream that pulls the logger from context during a Delete call loses the name/kind/method fields, producing inconsistent log output for Delete versus the other operations.

findings.title: Mode3 tests never verify the asynchronous Legacy write actually happens
findings.body: Mode 3's defining new behavior is firing an async write to Legacy storage after a successful Storage write (Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection). None of the updated tests synchronize with or assert on the Legacy mock being invoked (no waitgroup/channel, no `AssertExpectations`/`AssertCalled` on the Legacy mock). Since the goroutine can run after the test function returns, these tests provide no actual coverage of the new async replication behavior and would not catch a regression that broke or removed the Legacy write.

findings.title: New mode3 integration test asserts legacy search results immediately after k8s writes, racing the async legacy replication
findings.body: The 'Do CRUD via k8s (and check that legacy api still works)' subtest (exercised against the newly added mode3 configurations 'with dual write (file, mode 3)' and 'with dual write (unified storage, mode 3)') creates playlists through the k8s/unified API, then immediately queries the legacy `/api/playlists` endpoint and `getFromBothAPIs` (legacy GET) and expects them to already reflect the just-created/updated data. Under Mode3, writes to Legacy storage are explicitly asynchronous ('safe measure' goroutine with up to a 10s timeout), so there is no guarantee the legacy copy has been written by the time these assertions run. This test has no retry/eventual-consistency handling and is likely to be flaky (intermittently failing in CI) specifically for the new mode3 configurations this PR adds.
